g.text: Secondary: diabetes GLP-1 (spillover outcome): overall ATT -0.8 (95% CI -4.2 to 2.7)
Secondary: Saxenda: overall ATT 0.2 (95% CI -0.3 to 0.7)
Primary: Wegovy/Zepbound (obesity_wz): overall ATT 12.2 (95% CI 8.4 to 16.0)
Dynamic ATT by quarters since coverage began, same design as the primary; each panel on its own y-scale; bars are
pointwise 95% CIs (simultaneous bands omitted: they are very wide with single-state cohorts); grey = fewer than 3
contributing states; leads before 2021 Q2 omitted.
Overall ATT per 1,000 enrollees: 12.2 (95% CI 8.4 to 16.0) for Wegovy/Zepbound, 0.2 (95% CI
-0.3 to 0.7) for Saxenda, -0.8 (95% CI -4.2 to 2.7) for diabetes GLP-1 products
The diabetes GLP-1 outcome is a pre-specified spillover outcome, not a clean negative control: a negative estimate is consistent with substitution
from off-label diabetes products to covered obesity products, a positive one with spillover in prescribing, and neither can be told apart from a
design problem with this data alone. Source: CMS State Drug Utilization Data and Medicaid enrollment (warehouse marts). Gross of rebates; counts under
